record.title: The Science of Scientific Writing
record.source_type: primary writing-guidance article; permission-posted retyped copy
record.notes: Inspected reader interpretation, subject–verb separation, topic/stress positions, context, and explicit caution that principles are not rules. Copy identifies original publication and permission to retype/post.

sources.title: Ten simple rules for structuring papers

record.title: Ten simple rules for structuring papers
record.notes: Inspected paragraph context/content/conclusion, parallelism, explicit support for repeating the same technical term, result logic, outlining and test-reader feedback (Rules 3–4 and 7–10).
record.limitations: Advice editorial, not a venue submission policy or causal study of acceptance. The proposed structure should not be universalized to every discipline, genre or paragraph. Reader teach-back procedure in the derived reference is our editorial design.

record.title: Ten simple rules for structuring papers
record.notes: Brett Mensh and Konrad Kording, published September 28, 2017. Inspected text of Rules 1–10, especially central contribution, terminology, abstract/introduction logic, evidence-linked results, discussion limitations, outlining, and reader feedback. Recommendations are expert editorial guidance, not a causal test of acceptance outcomes.
record.limitations: Did not audit every cited reference or visually inspect linked figure/table assets. A linked November 2017 correction was visible but its contents were not inspected; no detail unique to the correction is used. The context-content-conclusion structure is treated as optional guidance rather than mandatory paragraph architecture.

sources.title: Ten simple rules to make your publication look better

record.title: Ten simple rules to make your publication look better
record.notes: Inspected Rules 3–4: domain nomenclature, stable identifiers, abbreviation introduction in abstract/body, independently readable displays and one abbreviation per term.
record.limitations: Illustrations concentrate on computational biology. Specific nomenclature must be checked against the present domain authority; this source does not establish a current universal abbreviation count or a paper-quality score.

record.title: The ASA Statement on p-Values: Context, Process, and Purpose
record.venue: The American Statistician 70(2):129-133; American Statistical Association
record.notes: Inspected the primary publisher-indexed statement: p-value definition, six principles and explanations, selective reporting, effect-size/importance distinction, alternative approaches, and conclusion. record.limitations: No claim of a locally archived publisher PDF. The statement does not ban p-values, supply every statistical method, or make nonsignificance equivalent to support for a null.

record.title: Reproducibility: let's get it right from the start
